div.l: And this figure he hadde therto
That if gold rust what shuld yren̄ do
For if a prest be foule on whom̄ we trust
No wundir is a lewde man̄ to rust
Shame it is and if a prest toke kepe
A shitten̄ Shepherd and a clene Shepe
Wel ought a prest ensample forto yeue
By his clennesse hough that a Shepe shuld lyue
He sette not his benefice to hire
And leve his Shepe encumbrid in the myre
And renne to londoıı̄un vnto seint poules
To seche him a Chauntry for soules ·
Or with a brethirhede to be witholde ·
But duellith at home and kepith wel his fold
So that the folk ne make it not mistery
He was a Shepherd ⁊and not a mercenary
And though he holy were and vertuous
He was not to synful men to despitous
Ne of his speche daungerous ne digne
But in his teching discrete and benyngne
To draw folk to heuen with feirnesse
By good ensample / this was his bisynesse
But if it were eny persone obstinate
What so he were of high or lowe estate
Him wold he snybbe sharply for the nones
A bettir prest I trow nowher none is
He waitid aft̉er no pompe ne reuerence
Ne makid him a spicid conscience
But cristis lore and his apostles twelue
He taught / but first he folowid it himselue
¶ With him ther was a plough man þat was hⁱis broþ̉er
That had y ladde of dunge fulle many a fothir
A true Swynker and a good was he
Lyuyng in peas and parfite charite
God loued he best with alle his hole hert
At alle times though him gramed or smert
And than his neighbour as himselue
He wold thressh and therto dike ⁊and delue ·
For cristis sake for euery pore wight ·
Wiþouten hyre if it lay in his myght ·
